react_result.final_narrative_text: The eight differentially abundant metabolites resolve into two tightly interconnected biological circuits. The dominant cross-paradigm signal is steroid hormone metabolism: all five sex-steroid compounds — dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), androstenedione, testosterone, estrone, and 17β-estradiol — co-enrich in the KEGG 'Steroid hormone biosynthesis' pathway (KEGG:hsa00140, MetaboAnalystR rank 0, p = 8.39×10⁻⁶) and in the WikiPathways 'Sulfatase and aromatase pathway' (WP:WP5368, RaMP FDR = 7.99×10⁻¹⁶, fold enrichment 2 757×). RaMP also reports them in the SMPDB 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (SMPDB:SMP00068), the KEGG-native 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (KEGG:map00150), and the Reactome 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' (REACT:R-HSA-196071), spanning six pathway databases. Mummichog independently ranks the MUMM network node 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' first (p = 1.68×10⁻⁴, 11/11 compounds matched), confirming this signal via m/z-direct empirical networking. The remaining three non-steroid compounds are secondary hits: indol-3-ylacetaldehyde maps to MUMM 'Tryptophan metabolism' (rank 3, p = 0.040) and (S)-3-hydroxyisobutyric acid appears in branched-chain amino-acid degradation and propanoate metabolism (p ≈ 0.044), both with weaker enrichment scores. Menadione (vitamin K₃) did not reach significance in any pathway and appears as an outlier in the input set. The five steroid driver metabolites are structurally validated and carry no InChIKey conflicts, confirming they represent five discrete chemical species converging on a single biological process.
